claim: tubamp's tremolo applies total gain sqrt(1-mix) + sqrt(mix)*(1 - depth*(1-lfo)) with lfo = 0.5+0.5*sin; at the defaults (depth 0.4, mix 0.35) that is 1.61 dB of tremolo with a +2.91 dB peak, and only mix = 1 lets depth = 1 reach zero gain

Guitar Rig 6 RigTremolo's LFO is a pulse (phase compared with a width threshold) slewed by a one-pole that uses one coefficient when the target is 1.0 and another when it is the floor; the output gain is that state
Guitar Rig 6 Tremolo rate is exponential in the knob: 0.4297 Hz at Rt=0.125, 2.0439 Hz at 0.5, 5.7810 Hz at 0.75, 16.354 Hz at 1 (= 0.2555*64^Rt)
Guitar Rig 6 Tremolo depth is linear gain: the floor is 1 - Intensity (0.7500, 0.5000, 0.2500, 0.1000) and Intensity 1 gives 0.0000

Guitar Rig 6 Tremolo slew corner is min(rate * 2^((60-95*knob)/12), 150 Hz): the 150.0 constant is 0x43160000 in onSetSampleRate, and the measured 10-90 % rise at Up=0 is 5.33 ms at 2.04 Hz and 2.35-2.38 ms at 5.78 Hz and above
where: Guitar Rig 6, NI::DSP::RigTremolo::onSetSampleRate 0x2e5f64 (0x2e5fd0-0x2e5fec) and setParamUp 0x2e61cc; evidence/gr6_tremolo_measure.tsv section A

claim: Guitar Rig 6 Tremolo Pan mode mirrors the left gain: envelope correlation -1.0000, gL+gR constant at 1.2500, gL^2+gR^2 between 0.7813 and 1.0608 (Intensity 0.75)

Guitar Rig 6 RigFender (Twang Reverb) vibrato: lamp lit while phase > 0.8 (constant 0xbf4ccccd), target 1 - depth*lit, one-pole coefficient chosen by the lit flag from two values, result multiplied into the signal
where: Guitar Rig 6, NI::DSP::RigFender::processBuffer 0x2c739c, instructions 0x2c79ec-0x2c7a54 (constant loaded at 0x2c7448)

claim: Guitar Rig 6 Twang Reverb vibrato measured at full intensity, -30 dBFS: gain falls in 12.06 ms and recovers in 33.9 ms (10-90 %), floor 0.117, loud 75 % of the cycle; rate 3.863 Hz .. 12.248 Hz
Guitar Rig 6 Twang Reverb vibrato depth shrinks when the amp is driven: 17.88 dB at -30 dBFS input, 11.16 dB at -6 dBFS (Intensity 1)
Guitar Rig 6 RigAC30 tremolo is A*(1-p^2) with alternating sign, ADDED to two lanes of the signal vector before the valve-table lookup (fadd.4s at 0x2bc980), not multiplied into the signal

Guitar Rig 6 AC Box tremolo depth depends on drive: Clean preset 1.86 dB at -30 dBFS and 1.57 dB at -6 dBFS; Crunch preset 3.79 dB at -30 dBFS and 1.22 dB at -6 dBFS; the gain swings above and below the no-tremolo level; rate 2.001 .. 7.003 Hz

AmpliTube 5 Tremolo stomp and FenderTremolo compute out = in*(1-depth) + in*lfo*depth with lfo from an interpolated static table; the tables bottom out at 0.172 (-15.3 dB) and 0.060 (-24.4 dB), so full depth is never silent

AmpliTube 5 calls FenderTremolo::Module::Process from four Fender amp PreAmp wrappers, and in the '65 Deluxe Reverb it is called after the tone-stack StateSpace and after SpringReverbAT3::Module::Process
where: AmpliTube 5, bl 0xcdc7a8 at 0x15d7c94, 0x15dd4a4, 0x162391c, 0x1629c48; in the symbol at 0x15d7c94: bl StateSpace at 0x15d7244, bl SpringReverbAT3 at 0x15d76dc

claim: AmpliTube 5 Shape Shifter: skewed phase, crossfade of a triangle with a raised-cosine or a square table, u = [0x20] - depth*lfo, a gain-law table that is a straight line in dB (slope 33.9 dB, floor -33.3 dB), then a one-pole low-pass built from 2*pi*100 Hz (0x441d1463), then out = in*gain

TONEX tremolo: rate = 0.1 + 9.9*knob Hz (2.575, 5.05, 7.5247, 10.0); LEVEL is a linear depth with floor 1-L and crest 1+0.414*L (square at L=1: 0.0000 .. 1.4142); SHAPE crossfades triangle to square; square edges take 4.79 ms; identical at -36, -18, -6 dBFS
TONEX TREM SPREAD offsets the right channel's LFO by 0 .. 180 degrees linearly (0.0, 45.0, 90.2, 135.1, 180.0 at 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1)

Fender harmonic vibrato splits the signal with single-stage RC filters: high-pass 250 pF + 1 M (about 636 Hz), low-pass 220 k + 5 nF (about 144 Hz), 6 dB/oct each, and modulates the two bands with LFO signals 180 degrees apart

claim: LDR optocouplers respond asymmetrically: VTL5C3 turn-on 2.5 ms to 63 % and turn-off 35 ms to 100 kOhm, NSL-32SR2 rise 5 ms and decay 80 ms; the DAFx-13 Buchla LPG paper models the vactrol as a low-pass whose response time is switched by the sign of the input's derivative (about 12 ms up, 250 ms down)
Proposed stereo law: raising a sine LFO shape to the power (1 - spread/360) makes the summed channel power constant at 180 degrees (-3.01 dB min and max), where the linear law dips to -6.02 dB
A 120 Hz one-pole on a square tremolo gain lowers the splatter of a 1 kHz carrier in the 3-6 kHz band from -41.9 dBc to -64.8 dBc and gives 2.92 ms edges
